chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of our companions, from Muhammad ibn al-Haytham, from Zayd Abu al-Hasan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one for whom the established fact is firm will not stand upon a lifeless doubt until he knows the ultimate limit, and seeks the newly emerging issue from the speaker from the inheritor, and by what thing you are ignorant of, what you denied, and by what thing you recognized what you visualized, if you are believers.'

key_terms.النَّاطِقُ عَنِ الْوَارِثِ: The speaker from the inheritor (referring to the Imams)
key_terms.مُنْتَهَى الْغَايَةِ: The ultimate limit / End of the matter

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim resolve religious doubts according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (as), establishes the epistemological principle of 'Haqiqah' (firm reality) as the antidote to 'Shubah' (doubtful matters), urging believers to trace knowledge back to the 'Natiq' (the speaking authority, i.e., the Imams) to avoid error. It highlights the Shia methodology of verifying religious claims by returning to the source of divine speech, ensuring that what is accepted or rejected is based on clear, authoritative evidence rather than speculation. This reinforces the concept of Tawbah and Taqwa through rigorous intellectual verification of faith tenets.
